create.name: New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care
create.bio:
This Soto Zen community in Manhattan joins meditation practice with care for people facing illness, ageing, grief and the end of life. It was founded in 2007 by Koshin Paley Ellison and Chodo Robert Campbell, recognised Zen teachers in the White Plum lineage who had both worked as chaplains, and who modelled it on the small neighbourhood temples they had visited in Japan. Paley Ellison, its abbot, is the author of Wholehearted and Untangled.

Zen practice runs alongside its training work. A daily online midday sitting with discussion runs Monday to Saturday, and on Sunday mornings and Monday and Wednesday evenings there is zazen, chanting and a Dharma talk, both at the zendo and on Zoom, with guidance for beginners twice a month. Half-day retreats, sesshin, ninety-day online practice periods, graduate-level classes on sutras and precepts and a two-year certificate programme in Soto Zen studies offer deeper study. Its care side trains chaplains, clinicians and volunteer caregivers and hosts support groups, and recorded talks by its teachers are published online.

courses.title: November Half-Day Retreat 2026
courses.description: A Saturday morning of silent sitting and walking meditation with a Dharma talk, open to all levels, held at the zendo with limited places and also online. In-person places must be reserved when registering.

courses.title: Certificate in Soto Zen Buddhist Studies
courses.description: A graduate-level programme of 36 credit hours combining study of Soto Zen texts, zazen and community learning, with courses online or in person and two silent retreats required. It can be completed in about two years and is open to people of any tradition or none.

courses.title: Online & In-Person Zendo
courses.description: The regular schedule of zazen: a weekday and Saturday midday sitting online with a short prompt and small-group discussion, and Sunday morning and Monday and Wednesday evening sessions with chanting and talks, at the zendo and on Zoom. Beginners receive guidance on the first and third Sundays.
courses.price: Offered free of charge; donations welcome

free_resources.title: An introduction to Zen Meditation
free_resources.description: An eight-part video course with Koshin Paley Ellison covering Zen history, posture, shikantaza, walking meditation, koans, sangha and bringing practice into daily life, free to watch for 48 hours after registering.

free_resources.title: Podcasts
free_resources.description: Recorded Dharma talks by the centre's guiding teachers and senior students on practice, precepts, care for oneself and others, and meeting suffering with steadiness.
